books.section: Topic 3.13 Continuity and Change in Period 3
Topic 3.12 Movement in the Early Republic

stimulus.text:
| Year | What happened |
|---|---|
| 1763 | Britain's Proclamation drew a line at the Appalachian Mountains and barred colonists from settling west of it. |
| 1783 | The Treaty of Paris ended the war. Britain gave the United States the land east of the Mississippi River, including the Ohio country. Native nations living there took no part in the treaty. |
| 1794 | At Fallen Timbers, General Wayne's army defeated a Native confederation. |
| 1795 | In the Treaty of Greenville, Native nations gave up claims to most of Ohio. |
stimulus.source_note: Barron's Premium 2027 Chapter 5, Topics 3.2 and 3.12; 5 Steps to a 5 2024 Chapter 11.

source: original; timeline compiled from Barron's Premium 2027 Chapter 5, Topics 3.2 and 3.12.
stem: What stayed the same across all four moments in the timeline?

options.text: Others decided Native claims to the land, not Native nations.
Native nations kept full control of the Ohio country.
options.misconception: By 1795 Native nations had given up claims to most of Ohio.

options.text: Settlers stopped crossing the Appalachian Mountains.
options.misconception: Settlers kept pushing west, which is why the land was contested.

options.text: Britain and the United States agreed to share Ohio.
options.misconception: Britain handed Ohio to the United States; the two did not share it.

rationales.A: Britain drew the line, Britain and the United States settled Ohio's fate, and the United States took the land, so Native nations never decided their own claims.
rationales.B: By 1795 Native nations had given up claims to most of Ohio.
rationales.C: Settlers kept pushing west, which is why the land was contested.
rationales.D: Britain handed Ohio to the United States; the two did not share it.
rationales.general:
1. In 1763 Britain drew the line; Native nations did not draw it.
2. In 1783 Britain and the United States settled Ohio's fate; Native nations took no part.
3. In 1794 and 1795 the United States took the land by victory and treaty.
4. In every moment, others decided Native claims to the land.
5. Resistance continued, but the decisions were never Native nations' own to make.
Remember: a continuity can be who decides, not only what happens.
